terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see the shop's rules applied to today's order.

tasks.title: Spot a big order
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/booleans.js`, make a `const` called `bigOrder`: `true` when `totalCents` is `freeShippingFromCents` or more, `false` otherwise. Print it.

Check runs your file with other orders, including one exactly on the line, and expects `true` or `false` itself.
nextSteps: Read the order and the rules near the top of the file.
Pick the comparison that means "or more".
Make `bigOrder` from that comparison of the two names.
hints: A comparison is already true or false. You can store it in a variable as it is.
There are two comparisons for "bigger": one leaves out the equal case and one includes it. The task includes it.
The line has the shape `const bigOrder = totalCents ... freeShippingFromCents`, with "bigger than or equal to" in place of the dots.

tasks.title: Decide on free shipping
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make a `const` called `freeShipping`. Shipping is free for a big order, or for any order whose `deliveryZone` is `'local'`. `freeShipping` is `true` when either is the case. Print it.

Check tries small and big orders in each delivery zone.
nextSteps: Make sure Task 1 passes: `bigOrder` is the first rule.
Write the second rule: is the zone the local one?
Join the two rules with the operator for "or".
Print it and try changing `deliveryZone` at the top to see it change.
hints: There are two rules, and one of them being true is enough.
To ask whether two values are the same, use `===`. The zone is text, so the value you compare it with needs quotes.
The line has the shape `const freeShipping = bigOrder || deliveryZone === '...'`, with the local zone's name in the quotes.

tasks.title: Can it ship today?
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make a `const` called `canShipToday`: `true` when there are at least as many candles in stock (`candlesInStock`) as the order needs (`quantity`), and the shop is not closed (`shopClosed`). Print it.

Check tries orders with enough stock, too little stock, a closed shop, and both problems at once.
nextSteps: Write the stock rule as one comparison.
Write the shop rule: you need the opposite of `shopClosed`.
Join the two with the operator for "and".
Print it and run the file.
hints: Both rules must hold at the same time for the order to ship.
`!` turns true into false and false into true. "At least as many" includes the equal case.
The line has the shape `const canShipToday = candlesInStock >= quantity && ...`, with the opposite of `shopClosed` in place of the dots.

tasks.title: Is there a gift note?
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make a `const` called `hasGiftNote`: `true` when `giftNote` has any text in it, `false` when it is empty text. It must be `true` or `false` itself, not the note. Print it.

Check tries an empty note, a long note and a note of one letter.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on truthy and falsy values.
Decide which kind empty text is.
Print it, then put a note in `giftNote` at the top and run it again.
hints: Every value is either truthy or falsy. Empty text is one of the few falsy ones.
The lesson shows a way to turn any value into the `true` or `false` it counts as.
`Boolean(...)` with `giftNote` in the brackets gives exactly the true or false you need.
